items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Freddie 'Snake Hips' Taylor and I lived in the same hotel and Freddie was hip to gage... I went to Freddie's room a few times

ctx.x: Later, during my sojourn in Paris, I met a handsome young quiet sax player from St. Louis, Missouri named Cle Sadler. We used to drink together in Lisieux's but I never heard him play.

Another famous personality that hung around the Lisieux was Spencer Williams, the composer of 'Basin Street Blues.' Kid Chocolate, the famous Cuban boxer was in Paris, so was Jimmie Monroe, the husband of Nina Ma McKinney who was one of the movie stars who played in the first all negro movie called 'Halleluiah'. Freddie 'Snake Hips' Taylor and I lived in the same hotel and Freddie was hip to gage as marijuana or reefers were called.

I went to Freddie's room a few times and it would be like walking into a London fog. The windows were closed and reefer smoke would be so thick that you could cut it with a knife. Freddie and Jimmie would be smoking and to my surprise Kid Chocolate was in the room also. I didn't see the Kid smoking but I thought that being in a closed room full of marijuana smoke was not good for a prize fighter but that was his business. I didn't smoke the stuff either after what it had done to me the night I saw Cecil Scott and…
